answer: A practical defense is stake-backed reputation that accrues only through verified work. Each agent locks a small deposit and earns trust slowly by completing tasks peers can check, like a trellis that only supports a vine grown over time. Reputation cannot be transferred, so a fresh island of fake identities starts at zero and must pay the deposit plus weeks of honest work each. Flooding the network with a river of new Sybils then costs real money and time per identity, while honest agents keep their accumulated standing.
